headline: Wall Street Eyes Iran Talks and Fresh Data After Records Close
body_html:
Futures point to a cautious open on Wednesday after the broad market capped Tuesday's session with fresh record highs on the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, powered by artificial-intelligence-linked earnings and growing optimism that Washington and Tehran may be closing in on a diplomatic agreement. President Trump described Tuesday as a full day of negotiation with Iran, calling the discussions very promising — language that sent the dollar softer overnight and nudged gold to its highest level in a month.

Oil extended its retreat in Asian and European trading as investors chose to wait for concrete terms before pricing in any supply relief, while the yen steadied after recent volatility. Red Sea tensions remained a live variable: Houthi forces claimed a strike on a Saudi tanker, and a projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel near Yemeni waters, though all crew were confirmed safe. Gulf shipping traffic held broadly steady, traders said.

On the data calendar, Wednesday's releases will be scrutinised for clues on the Federal Reserve's next move. Semiconductor names lead the sector scorecard heading into the open, and the earnings tape remains heavy — earnings guidance language around geopolitics will command particular attention from desk traders today.

briefs.headline: Iran Talks Dominate Macro Mood Ahead of Open
briefs.body: President Trump confirmed that US and Iranian officials spent the entirety of Tuesday in negotiations, describing the tone as very good. The prospect of a deal softened the dollar in overnight trading and lifted gold to a one-month peak, signalling that risk sentiment is being shaped more by diplomacy than by data at the moment.

briefs.headline: Oil Slips as Traders Withhold Judgment on Mideast Deal
briefs.body: Crude prices extended their decline into Wednesday's pre-market session as investors declined to front-run a US-Iran agreement that remains unsigned. China's decision to ease fuel-export controls for a second consecutive month added modest supply-side pressure, keeping energy bulls on the defensive ahead of the New York open.

briefs.headline: Red Sea Remains a Flashpoint Despite Peace Optimism
briefs.body: Houthi forces claimed responsibility for an attack on a Saudi oil tanker in the Red Sea, and a separate projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel in nearby Yemeni waters — though Indian authorities confirmed all seafarers were rescued safely. Gulf shipping traffic held steady overall, but the incidents underscore that route risk has not dissipated.

briefs.headline: Zebra Technologies Surges More Than 26% on Earnings Beat
briefs.body: Zebra Technologies was Tuesday's standout performer in our universe, jumping 26.47% after the tech-hardware company delivered results that sharply exceeded expectations. The move was the largest single-session gain among tracked names and signals that enterprise hardware demand may be firming more quickly than the market had assumed.

briefs.headline: Bruker Slumps Nearly 22% as Life-Science Tools Disappoint
briefs.body: Bruker led Tuesday's decliners, tumbling 21.79% in the sharpest single-session drop among tracked names. The life-science tools maker's results fell well short of expectations, reviving concerns about capital-spending caution among research and laboratory customers that have weighed on the broader healthcare-instruments group this year.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Sector Tops Tuesday's Sector Leaderboard
briefs.body: Semiconductors posted a 7.11% advance on Tuesday — the strongest gain of any sector in our tracked universe — fuelled in part by Arm Holdings' 17.36% surge following its earnings report. The sector's outperformance lifted the overall breadth picture, with 433 of 549 names in our universe closing higher against just 115 decliners.
